title: Every pairing
prompt: Show every student's name with every course title. Replace the ___.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring');

solutions: SELECT s.name, c.title FROM students s CROSS JOIN courses c;

title: Grid size
prompt: Show how many rows a cross join of customers and products gives, as grid_rows.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT COUNT(*) AS grid_rows FROM customers CROSS JOIN products;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS grid_rows FROM customers;
SELECT COUNT(*) AS grid_rows FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id;

title: Every customer and status
prompt: Show every customer's name with every different order status, as status.
hints: Cross join with a DISTINCT subquery.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (14, 7, '2024-04-01', 'returned');

solutions: SELECT c.name, s.status FROM customers c CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT status FROM orders) s;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT c.name, o.status FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id;
SELECT c.name, s.status FROM customers c CROSS JOIN orders s;

title: Attempts per pair
prompt: For every student and course, show the student's name, the course title, and how many times they enrolled, as attempts. Pairs with none show 0.
hints: Cross join, then LEFT JOIN enrolments.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring');

solutions: SELECT s.name, c.title, COUNT(e.id) AS attempts FROM students s CROSS JOIN courses c LEFT JOIN enrolments e ON e.student_id = s.id AND e.course_id = c.id GROUP BY s.id, s.name, c.id, c.title;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT s.name, c.title, COUNT(*) AS attempts FROM students s CROSS JOIN courses c LEFT JOIN enrolments e ON e.student_id = s.id AND e.course_id = c.id GROUP BY s.id, s.name, c.id, c.title;
SELECT s.name, c.title, COUNT(e.id) AS attempts FROM students s JOIN enrolments e ON e.student_id = s.id JOIN courses c ON c.id = e.course_id GROUP BY s.id, s.name, c.id, c.title;

title: Empty combinations
prompt: Show each customer's name and product name pair where that customer has never bought that product, for customer 1 only.
hints: Cross join, LEFT JOIN purchases, and keep NULLs.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: UPDATE orders SET customer_id = 1 WHERE id = 2;

solutions: SELECT c.name, p.name AS product FROM customers c CROSS JOIN products p LEFT JOIN (SELECT o.customer_id, i.product_id FROM orders o JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id) b ON b.customer_id = c.id AND b.product_id = p.id WHERE c.id = 1 AND b.product_id IS NULL;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT c.name, p.name AS product FROM customers c CROSS JOIN products p WHERE c.id = 1;
SELECT c.name, p.name AS product FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id WHERE c.id = 1;

title: Sales in every category per month
prompt: For every month in orders and every product category, show month, category, and total units sold as units, with 0 for none.
hints: Build the grid from two DISTINCT lists.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT m.month, k.category, COALESCE(SUM(s.quantity), 0) AS units FROM (SELECT DISTINCT strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) AS month FROM orders) m CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT category FROM products) k LEFT JOIN (SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', o.order_date) AS month, p.category, i.quantity FROM orders o JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id) s ON s.month = m.month AND s.category = k.category GROUP BY m.month, k.category;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', o.order_date) AS month, p.category, SUM(i.quantity) AS units FROM orders o JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id GROUP BY month, p.category;

SELECT m.month, k.category, SUM(s.quantity) AS units FROM (SELECT DISTINCT strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) AS month FROM orders) m CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT category FROM products) k LEFT JOIN (SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', o.order_date) AS month, p.category, i.quantity FROM orders o JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id) s ON s.month = m.month AND s.category = k.category GROUP BY m.month, k.category;

title: Report card grid
prompt: For every student and subject, show the student's name, the subject, and a label named status: Taken if they've enrolled in any course of it, otherwise Not taken.
hints: Cross join students with distinct subjects.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring');

solutions: SELECT s.name, k.subject, CASE WHEN COUNT(e.id) > 0 THEN 'Taken' ELSE 'Not taken' END AS status FROM students s CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT subject FROM courses) k LEFT JOIN courses c ON c.subject = k.subject LEFT JOIN enrolments e ON e.course_id = c.id AND e.student_id = s.id GROUP BY s.id, s.name, k.subject;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT s.name, c.subject, 'Taken' AS status FROM students s JOIN enrolments e ON e.student_id = s.id JOIN courses c ON c.id = e.course_id GROUP BY s.id, s.name, c.subject;

SELECT s.name, k.subject, CASE WHEN COUNT(*) > 0 THEN 'Taken' ELSE 'Not taken' END AS status FROM students s CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT subject FROM courses) k LEFT JOIN courses c ON c.subject = k.subject LEFT JOIN enrolments e ON e.course_id = c.id AND e.student_id = s.id GROUP BY s.id, s.name, k.subject;
